page.description:
Page number for pagination.

Specifies the page of results to retrieve, with '1' being the first page.

Must be a positive integer.

Used to navigate through paginated results when the dataset exceeds the page's maximum size, preventing overly large responses.

Page size is controlled by the 'limit' parameter.

This pagination mechanism is critical for system performance and reliability. It prevents overwhelming the system with large data transfers, reduces network latency, and provides a structured approach to handling large datasets. Administrators can page through complete results lists, enabling comprehensive review of all session records without exceeding resource limits.

limit.description:
Number of sessions per page.

Controls the size of each page of results.

Range: 1 to 100 inclusive.

Default: 20.

Provides performance optimization by limiting the amount of data transmitted per request while allowing clients to adjust based on their specific UI needs.

This parameter is essential for balancing data completeness with system performance. Very large limits could degrade database performance and increase response times, while very small limits would require excessive paging operations. The configurable range of 1-100 allows system administrators to find the optimal balance between usability and performance for different use cases.

The default value of 20 is chosen to provide sufficient information per page without overwhelming the user interface or the system.

search.description:
Full-text search across session metadata.

Performs a case-insensitive search across all session fields including user_id, token, and metadata.

Helps find sessions when exact identifiers are unknown, such as searching for sessions associated with a partial user email or token substring.

Matches any occurrence of the search term within any text field of the session record.

For security investigations, this field enables discovery of sessions even when only partial or incomplete identifying information is available. Administrators can search for sessions by partial user identifiers, device names, IP addresses, or other partial metadata, significantly enhancing forensic investigation capabilities.

ITodoListUserSession.ISummary.description:
Summary information for user authentication sessions, optimized for list displays and administrative monitoring. This schema includes essential session metadata without exposing sensitive authentication tokens or secrets.

Used in the PATCH /todoList/user/sessions operation to provide paginated results showing session status, creation time, expiration, and activity tracking. The schema follows strict security conventions by omitting all JWT tokens, encryption keys, or authentication secrets.

Session summary data is presented with contextual information for security audits while maintaining privacy boundaries - allowing administrators to identify active sessions, detect potential compromise, and review user authentication patterns without accessing sensitive credentials. This summary view is performance-optimized for list rendering and system monitoring, with all fields derived directly from the todo_list_user_sessions database table.

System Integration Context:
- Retrieved through the /todoList/user/sessions endpoint for administrative licensing and security reporting
- Used by security teams for session lifecycle analysis and threat detection
- Integrated into audit trails alongside user activity logs and authentication events

Privacy and Security Considerations:
- Deliberately excludes raw authentication tokens and cryptographic secrets
- Privacy-compliant by design - does not expose personally identifiable information beyond user identifier
- Meets regulatory requirements for session monitoring without over-collection of sensitive data

Business Implications:
- Enables administrators to detect anomalous authentication patterns
- Supports security incident response through session history analysis
- Facilitates compliance auditing with timestamped authentication events
- Provides data for session-based license management

This summary representation is intentionally constrained to operational metadata that supports system integrity and security monitoring without compromising user privacy or security boundaries.

id.description: Unique identifier for the session record in the todo_list_user_sessions table. Used for tracking and referencing specific authentication sessions in administrative interfaces and audit logs.

user_id.description: The associated todo_list_user identifier that created this session. Links to the user's authentication identity and enables secure association between sessions and user accounts. When combined with IP address and user agent data, this facilitates user behavior analysis and security incident detection.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this authentication session was first established. Follows ISO 8601 format and represents session origin time. Critical for determining session age, ongoing activity, and expiration status. Used in security policies to enforce session timeouts and detect prolonged or inappropriate authentication patterns.

expires_at.description: Timestamp when this session will expire. After this point, the session is no longer valid and must be refreshed or re-authenticated. Used in automated session cleanup processes and security alerting systems to identify sessions that are approaching expiration or have exceeded maximum lifetime.

last_activity.description: Timestamp of the most recent activity in this session. Used to determine session activity status and identify inactive sessions for cleanup. Key metric for detecting stale sessions that may indicate abandoned devices or compromised credentials. Used in conjunction with created_at to calculate total session duration.

oneOf.description: Current state of the authentication session. Active sessions are currently valid and may be used to authenticate requests. This is the standard state for recently authenticated sessions and active user work sessions.

Current state of the authentication session. Expired sessions have surpassed their designated lifespan and are no longer valid for authenticating requests. These sessions are automatically deactivated and cannot be renewed without fresh authentication.

Current state of the authentication session. Revoked sessions have been manually terminated by an administrator or through administrative policy. These sessions are immediately invalidated regardless of their original expiration time and are indicative of security actions such as password changes or suspicious behavior detection.

status.description: Current state of the authentication session. Determines whether a session is active for authentication purposes, has expired due to time limits, or has been manually revoked for security reasons.

ip_address.description: IP address from which this session was initiated. Used for security auditing, geographic tracking of authentication events, and fraud detection. Records the client's public IP address at the time of authentication session creation to support incident investigation and security compliance requirements.

user_agent.description: User agent string identifying the device and browser used to create this session. Helps identify client platforms and detect anomalous access patterns such as bot activity, automated credential stuffing, or unexpected device types. Useful for detecting fraud patterns, enforcing device-based access policies, and supporting customer support investigations.

ITodoListUserSession.description:
User session entity representing an active authentication session for a todo list user.

This schema defines the complete structure of a user session record stored in the todo_list_user_sessions database table. Each session represents an authenticated connection between a user and the system, containing metadata about the session's creation, activity, and termination.

Session records are automatically created upon successful user authentication and purged after a configurable expiration period for security compliance. The session data is used to validate JWT tokens and maintain user authentication state across requests.

This schema is used exclusively in response bodies for operations that retrieve or confirm session information, such as GET /todoList/user/sessions/{sessionId}. It is not used in request bodies, as session data is managed server-side based on authentication tokens.

When used in API responses, this schema provides users with transparency about their active authentication state, including session timestamps and associated user context.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user session record in the todo_list_user_sessions table. This UUID is generated automatically upon session creation and serves as the primary key for the session record.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when this session was created and activated. This corresponds to the moment when the user successfully authenticated and a new session record was generated in the database. The timestamp follows ISO 8601 format with UTC timezone.

last_activity_at.description: Timestamp indicating the most recent activity within this session. This field is updated every time the user makes a valid request with an associated valid JWT token. Used to track session inactivity and determine when to automatically expire an inactive session.

expires_at.description: Timestamp indicating when this session will automatically expire and be deleted from the system. Sessions are designed to expire after a configurable period of inactivity, ensuring security by terminating dormant connections. This field is set at session creation based on the system's session lifetime configuration.

is_active.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this session is currently active and valid. This flag is automatically set to false when a session expires or is manually terminated by a delete operation, but remains true while the session is active and has not reached its expiration time.
